summary: Ohio State returns from its bye to visit USC. Sayin remains out indefinitely in Day’s reported update; the quarterback plan, pass protection and USC’s downfield threats lead the week.

items.headline: Day says Sayin is out indefinitely
items.tldr: Day put Fahey ahead of St. Clair while leaving room for competition during the bye. Treat the next starter and the length of Sayin’s absence as separate questions.

items.headline: USC’s passing threats lead the opponent preview
items.tldr: Eleven Warriors examines Maiava and the Trojans’ receivers. Watch how Ohio State carries routes beyond the first break without opening a scramble lane.

items.headline: Ohio State’s last outing was a 19-15 win at Indiana
items.tldr: The Buckeyes return from an open date after a close road win. The next offense needs a protection plan that makes its quarterback’s first decision usable.

items.headline: Ohio State–USC kicks at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC
items.tldr: Saturday’s trip to Los Angeles has an evening Eastern viewing window. Keep the travel-day clock separate from the local kickoff time.

items.headline: USC falls 24-7 at Wisconsin before hosting Ohio State
items.tldr: The Trojans enter the matchup after a difficult offensive outing. Use the film to inspect protection and rushing lanes, without assuming the next game will follow the same script.

lead.headline: Make the first read usable.
lead.body: Give the next quarterback a clear throw and a protected launch point. Pair that with a run game that earns useful downs, while the defense keeps USC’s receivers in front of its help.

matchup.thesis: Simplify the decision without surrendering ambition
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Let protection, route spacing and the release work together. Take the clean completion, then choose the downfield shot when the pocket and coverage actually permit it.

signals.title: Quarterback plan
signals.summary: Separate preparation from a final call
signals.detail: Watch the confirmed starter, the opening formations and the first pressure answer. Do not turn a reported depth-chart edge into a season-long personnel decision.

signals.title: Up front: pass protection
signals.detail: Keep the pocket’s width and the receiving outlet connected. A free rusher should produce an immediate answer rather than an extended retreat.

signals.title: Rushing efficiency
signals.detail: Watch the block at the point of attack and the runner’s first cut. Useful early carries should make the passing plan easier to execute.

signals.title: Downfield coverage
signals.summary: Carry the route through the break
signals.detail: Keep leverage on the outside receiver while the safety tracks the deeper route. Close the pocket without letting the quarterback buy an uncovered throw.
